text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear claim in the opening sentence","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"The essay states its position right away and makes the argument easy to follow from the start."},{"evidence":"“if there is a problem such as a work zone or an accident, then the driver must take over”","quality":"source-based support","description":"It uses a relevant detail from the article to justify its point instead of relying on opinion alone."},{"evidence":"“Current driving laws make driverless cars illegal in most states” and “who is at fault”","quality":"argument development","description":"It develops the case with concrete policy and liability concerns that strengthen the reasoning."},{"evidence":"three short body paragraphs with separate points","quality":"organization","description":"The ideas are arranged in a clear structure that moves from technology to roads to laws."},{"evidence":"“Driverless cars can take the ease off the driver”","quality":"control of expression","description":"The writing is generally clearer and more polished, with fewer distracting errors that interrupt meaning."}]}
